questions.question: Who is the poet of “How to Tell Wild Animals”?
questions.explanation: The poem is a humorous description of how to identify different wild animals.

questions.question: Where might you encounter a wild animal according to the poem?
questions.explanation: The poet begins by imagining a person encountering wild animals in the eastern region.

questions.question: Which animal is described as having tawny skin?
questions.explanation: The Asian Lion is described as having a large tawny body.

questions.question: What will the tiger do if it encounters you?
questions.explanation: The tiger is identified by the way it attacks and eats its victim.

questions.question: Which animal is described as having black spots?
questions.explanation: The leopard is recognised by its spotted coat.

questions.question: What does the leopard do when it meets a person?

options.C: It leaps on the person again and again

questions.explanation: The repeated attack is part of the poem's humorous identification method.

questions.question: Which animal is described as hugging a person?
questions.explanation: The bear is humorously identified by its “hug.”

questions.question: Which animal is associated with a smile in the poem?
questions.explanation: The poet humorously connects the hyena with its laughing or smiling appearance.

questions.question: Which animal is associated with a “smile” showing its teeth?
questions.explanation: The crocodile is described as appearing to smile while actually showing its teeth.

questions.question: What is the main feature of “How to Tell Wild Animals”?

options.A: Humour and playful descriptions of wild animals

questions.explanation: The poet uses exaggeration and humour to describe how different animals can supposedly be identified.

questions.question: Why does the poet use a humorous tone while describing dangerous animals?

options.A: To suggest that wild animals are harmless
options.B: To make the poem entertaining while describing their characteristics
options.D: To make the animals look beautiful

questions.explanation: The poet presents dangerous encounters in a playful and exaggerated way.

questions.question: How can the Asian Lion be identified according to the poem?

options.A: By its tawny colour and its dangerous attack

questions.explanation: The poet describes the lion's tawny appearance and the danger of meeting it.

questions.question: What makes the description of the Bengal Tiger humorous?

options.A: The tiger is afraid of humans
options.B: The tiger runs away from everyone
options.C: The poet says that its identification may happen only after it has attacked you
options.D: The tiger is shown as a friendly pet

questions.explanation: The dangerous situation is presented in a deliberately comic manner.

questions.question: What is the most noticeable feature used to identify the leopard?
questions.explanation: The leopard's spotted coat is an important identifying feature.

questions.question: Why is the word “leaps” important in the description of the leopard?

options.B: It shows that the leopard is playful
options.C: It shows that the leopard is afraid
options.D: It shows the leopard's method of attacking its victim

questions.explanation: The repeated leaping is used humorously as a clue to identify the leopard.

questions.question: How is the bear identified in the poem?

options.C: By its habit of hugging its victim

questions.explanation: The poet humorously calls the bear's attack a “hug.”

questions.question: Why is the bear's attack called a “hug”?

options.B: Because the bear wants to make friends
options.C: To turn a dangerous attack into a humorous image

questions.explanation: The poet uses an ordinary friendly word for a dangerous action, creating humour.

questions.question: How does the poet describe the hyena?
questions.explanation: The hyena's facial expression is humorously compared with a smile.

questions.question: What makes the crocodile's description different from the hyena's?

options.A: The crocodile's smile is associated with tears

questions.explanation: The poet refers humorously to the crocodile's “tears” while describing its smile.

questions.question: What poetic technique is especially important in the poem?
questions.explanation: Dangerous animal encounters are described using playful, ironic expressions.

questions.question: What is the main reason the poet describes dangerous situations in a playful way?

options.A: To encourage people to approach wild animals
options.C: To prove that wild animals are harmless
options.D: To make the poem humorous and entertaining

questions.explanation: The poet turns dangerous encounters into comic descriptions.

questions.question: The descriptions of the lion, tiger and leopard mainly emphasize:

options.B: Their ability to live with humans

questions.explanation: Their actions toward a person are used as humorous clues for identifying them.

questions.question: Why is the expression describing the bear as giving a “hug” effective?

options.B: It proves that the bear is a trained animal
options.C: It uses a friendly expression for a dangerous action
options.D: It shows that bears love humans

questions.explanation: The contrast between a friendly “hug” and a dangerous attack creates humour.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the poet's treatment of the hyena and crocodile?

options.B: The poet uses their facial expressions to create humorous identification clues
options.C: Both animals are shown as harmless
options.D: The poet considers them more beautiful than other animals

questions.explanation: The hyena's smile and crocodile's tears are presented playfully as ways to recognise them.

questions.question: Which statement best expresses the deeper idea of the poem?

options.A: Scientific knowledge is unnecessary for understanding animals
options.B: Wild animals are less dangerous than domestic animals
options.C: Wild animals should always be approached closely to identify them
options.D: Animal identification can be presented through humour, exaggeration and memorable characteristics

questions.explanation: The poem does not give a scientific guide; it uses comic situations and distinctive animal traits to make identification memorable.

questions.question: Who is the poet of “The Ball Poem”?
questions.explanation: John Berryman wrote The Ball Poem.

questions.question: What has the boy lost?
questions.explanation: The poem begins with the boy watching his ball bounce away.

questions.question: Where does the ball go?
questions.explanation: The ball rolls and bounces toward the water and is lost.

questions.question: How does the boy feel after losing the ball?
questions.explanation: The loss of the ball causes the boy to experience sadness.

questions.question: What does the boy stand and watch?
questions.explanation: He watches helplessly as the ball moves away from him.

questions.question: What does the poet say the boy is learning?

options.D: How to buy a new ball

questions.explanation: Losing the ball becomes a lesson about experiencing loss.

questions.question: What does the ball symbolize in the poem?
questions.explanation: The ball represents something the child loves and is emotionally attached to.

questions.question: Why doesn't the poet simply offer the boy money for another ball?

options.A: He wants the boy to understand the experience of loss
options.B: The boy does not like new balls

questions.explanation: A replacement ball cannot remove the emotional experience of losing something loved.

questions.question: What important experience does the boy face?
questions.explanation: The loss teaches him an important lesson about life.

questions.question: What is the central idea of the poem?

options.A: Losing things is part of growing up and learning to accept loss
options.B: Playing with a ball is dangerous
options.D: Children should never play near water

questions.explanation: The poem uses the lost ball to show the child's first experience of understanding loss.

questions.question: Why is the boy deeply affected by losing the ball?

options.B: The ball has emotional value for him
options.D: He has lost his school bag

questions.explanation: The boy is attached to the ball, so its loss affects him emotionally.

questions.question: What does the phrase “epistemology of loss” mean?

options.A: Understanding what it means to experience loss

questions.explanation: The boy is beginning to understand, through experience, what loss means.

questions.question: Why can't another ball completely replace the lost ball?

options.C: The lost ball has emotional memories attached to it
options.D: The new ball will be smaller

questions.explanation: The value of the lost ball is not merely its price; the boy's attachment makes it special.

questions.question: What does the boy's reaction suggest about childhood?

options.A: Children can form strong emotional attachments to ordinary objects
options.D: Children never become emotionally attached to things

questions.explanation: The boy's sadness shows his emotional connection with the ball.

questions.question: What larger lesson does the boy begin to learn through the loss?

options.A: Toys are more important than people
options.B: Everything lost can immediately be replaced
options.D: Loss is a natural part of life

questions.explanation: The lost ball becomes a lesson in accepting loss.

questions.question: Why does the poet allow the boy to experience the loss instead of immediately comforting him?

options.A: The poet is angry with him
options.B: The poet does not care about the boy
options.C: The poet wants the boy to learn to deal with loss himself
options.D: The poet wants the boy to buy another ball

questions.explanation: Experiencing loss helps the child develop emotional understanding and maturity.

questions.question: What does the phrase “money is external” suggest?

options.A: Money has no value at all
options.C: Money cannot replace the emotional value of something personally lost
options.D: The boy has plenty of money

questions.explanation: Money can buy another ball, but it cannot restore the particular attachment to the lost one.

questions.question: How does the lost ball become a symbol of growing up?

options.B: It teaches the boy to play a new game
options.D: It introduces him to the experience of loss and acceptance

questions.explanation: Understanding that some things cannot simply be recovered is part of growing up.

questions.question: What is the significance of the poet's decision not to interfere immediately?

options.A: It allows the boy to learn an important life lesson through personal experience
options.B: It shows that the boy is responsible for the poet's loss
options.C: It shows that the poet dislikes children
options.D: It means the ball is unimportant

questions.explanation: The poet recognises that the boy needs to experience and understand loss rather than have it instantly removed.

questions.question: Which sequence best represents the boy's experience in the poem?
questions.explanation: The boy loses something he values, feels the pain of the loss, and begins learning how to cope with it.

questions.question: Why does the poet say that the boy is learning the “epistemology of loss”?

options.A: He is learning the price of different balls
options.B: He is learning how to earn money
options.C: He is learning how to prevent accidents
options.D: He is gaining personal understanding of what loss feels like

questions.explanation: The boy is experiencing loss directly, which gives him an understanding that cannot simply be taught through words.

questions.question: What does the lost ball represent beyond the physical object?

options.C: The boy's childhood attachment and his first experience of loss

questions.explanation: The ball becomes a symbol of something loved that cannot always be recovered.

questions.question: Why is the poet's decision not to offer money immediately important?

options.A: It makes the boy more interested in games
options.B: It proves that the ball was worthless
options.C: It allows the boy to develop an understanding of loss through experience
options.D: It shows that the poet has no money

questions.explanation: The poet understands that replacing the object would not teach the deeper lesson about accepting loss.

questions.question: What contrast is central to the poem?

options.B: Childhood innocence and the difficult reality of loss

questions.explanation: The child's simple attachment to the ball leads him into a more mature understanding of life's losses.

questions.question: Which interpretation best captures the deeper message of the poem?

options.A: Material possessions are more important than emotions
options.B: Children should avoid playing with valuable objects
options.C: Every lost object should immediately be replaced with money
options.D: Experiencing loss is part of growing up and learning to accept that some things cannot be recovered

questions.explanation: The lost ball becomes a small but meaningful lesson about loss, acceptance, and maturity.

questions.question: Who is the poet of “The Trees”?
questions.explanation: Adrienne Rich wrote The Trees.

questions.question: Where are the trees in the poem?
questions.explanation: The poem presents the trees as being confined inside a house and trying to move out.

questions.question: What are the trees trying to do?
questions.explanation: The trees are moving towards the outside world.

questions.question: What does the moonlight shine through?
questions.explanation: The poem describes the moon shining through the branches as the trees move out.

questions.question: What is happening to the roots?

options.B: They are working to free themselves

questions.explanation: The roots are described as moving and pushing against the cracks in the floor.

questions.question: What are the small twigs doing?

options.A: Making a sound like a bird

questions.explanation: The twigs are shown moving towards the glass, trying to get outside.

questions.question: What is happening to the leaves?

options.B: They are moving towards the glass

questions.explanation: The leaves strain towards the glass as the trees attempt to escape.

questions.question: What does the forest represent in the poem?

options.A: A place of freedom for the trees

questions.explanation: The trees belong naturally in the forest rather than inside the house.

questions.question: What is the poet doing while the trees move out?
questions.explanation: The poet watches the trees' movement and describes it.

questions.question: What is the central idea of “The Trees”?

options.A: Nature seeks freedom from human confinement

questions.explanation: The poem uses trees trying to escape a house as a symbol of the desire for freedom.

questions.question: Why do the trees struggle to move out of the house?

options.A: They are too weak to grow
options.B: They have been confined inside and must break through the barriers
options.C: They do not know where the forest is
options.D: They are afraid of the moonlight

questions.explanation: The roots, leaves and branches are shown struggling against the house's restrictions.

questions.question: What does the movement of the roots suggest?

options.A: The trees are actively trying to free themselves
options.B: The trees are trying to establish themselves deeper inside the house
options.C: The trees are preparing for winter

questions.explanation: The roots push against the cracks in the floor as part of the trees' escape.

questions.question: What is suggested by the trees' branches moving towards the glass?

options.C: Their desire to reach the outside world

questions.explanation: The movement towards the glass symbolises the trees' urge for freedom.

questions.question: Why is the forest described as waiting?

options.A: The forest is personified as expecting the trees to return
options.C: The forest is being cut down

questions.explanation: The poet gives the forest a human-like quality to emphasize that the trees naturally belong there.

questions.question: What does the phrase “the forest that was empty all these days” suggest?

options.A: The trees have forgotten the forest
options.B: There have never been trees in forests
options.D: The trees naturally belong in the forest and have been absent from it

questions.explanation: Their return restores the natural relationship between trees and forest.

questions.question: How does the poem personify the trees?

options.A: It treats them only as objects
options.C: It gives them human-like desires and actions

questions.explanation: The trees are shown struggling, moving, and seeking freedom like living beings with intentions.

questions.question: What does the house represent in the poem?
questions.explanation: The house prevents the trees from living in their natural environment.

questions.question: Why does the poet mention the moon?

options.B: To explain the phases of the moon
options.C: To show that the trees need moonlight to grow
options.D: To create a natural setting and show the trees moving into the outside world

questions.explanation: Moonlight helps create the transition from the confined indoor space to the natural world outside.

questions.question: What does the poet's act of writing while the trees escape suggest?

options.A: She is observing and recording a significant transformation
options.B: She is afraid of the forest
options.C: She is unaware of the trees
options.D: She wants to stop the trees

questions.explanation: The poet watches the trees' movement and documents their return to freedom.

questions.question: Which contrast is most important in the poem?
questions.explanation: The house represents confinement, while the forest represents the trees' natural freedom.

questions.question: What does the movement of the trees from the house to the forest symbolically represent?

options.D: The return of nature to its natural freedom

questions.explanation: The trees leave the confined indoor space and return to the forest where they naturally belong.

questions.question: Why does the poet describe the trees as if they are struggling like human beings?

options.A: To show that trees are weak
options.B: To make the poem a story about people
options.C: To personify nature and emphasize its desire for freedom

questions.explanation: Human-like actions make the trees' struggle against confinement more vivid.

questions.question: What is the significance of the house becoming empty as the trees leave?

options.A: It means the forest has disappeared
options.B: It shows that the poet dislikes the house
options.C: It emphasizes that the trees were never truly meant to remain confined there
options.D: It shows that the house has become more beautiful

questions.explanation: Their departure restores the natural order: trees belong outside in the forest.

questions.question: Which idea is most strongly conveyed through the repeated images of roots, leaves and branches moving outward?

options.A: Trees are unable to grow naturally
options.B: Nature continuously seeks its rightful space and freedom
options.D: Human beings control all aspects of nature

questions.explanation: Every part of the tree is shown working towards escape, reinforcing the theme of freedom.

questions.question: Which statement best expresses the deeper message of “The Trees”?

options.A: Forests are less important than houses
options.B: Confinement is necessary for the protection of trees
options.C: Nature can be permanently controlled by humans
options.D: Living beings have a natural urge to break free from restrictions and return to their rightful environment

questions.explanation: The trees' escape becomes a symbolic expression of freedom and resistance to confinement.

questions.question: Who is the poet of “Animals”?
questions.explanation: Walt Whitman wrote the poem “Animals”.

questions.question: With whom does the poet wish to live?
questions.explanation: The poet says he thinks he could turn and live with animals.

questions.question: What does the poet say he can do with animals?
questions.explanation: He expresses a wish to live among animals because he finds them contented and uncomplicated.

questions.question: How long does the poet say he has been sick of?
questions.explanation: The poet says he has been sick of the complexities of human society.

questions.question: What quality of animals does the poet admire first?
questions.explanation: He admires their calm, self-contained way of living.

questions.question: What do animals not do about their condition?
questions.explanation: The poet notes that animals do not complain about their condition.

questions.question: What do animals not discuss with the poet?
questions.explanation: The animals do not discuss or complain about their condition.

questions.question: What do animals not have to do for hours?

options.A: Stand and sweat in the dark about their sins

questions.explanation: The poet contrasts animals with humans who worry about their sins and duties.

questions.question: What quality does the poet say animals possess that humans often lack?
questions.explanation: The poet admires the animals’ contentment.

questions.question: What does the poet wish to do after observing animals?
questions.explanation: He is attracted by their uncomplicated way of life and wants to learn from them.

questions.question: Why does the poet feel more comfortable with animals than with humans?

options.D: Animals are contented and free from many human complications

questions.explanation: He finds animals contented, calm and free from the anxieties that trouble humans.

questions.question: What does “not one is dissatisfied” suggest?

options.B: Animals appear content with their natural lives

questions.explanation: The poet sees animals as satisfied with their natural existence.

questions.question: What human weakness is suggested by the animals’ lack of complaint?

options.C: Humans often become dissatisfied with what they have

questions.explanation: The contrast suggests that human beings often create dissatisfaction through their desires and worries.

questions.question: Why does the poet mention “the mania of owning things”?

options.C: To criticize human obsession with possession and wealth

questions.explanation: The poet criticizes the human desire to own and accumulate things.

questions.question: What does the poet admire about animals’ relationship with their surroundings?

options.D: They are at ease with their natural existence

questions.explanation: Animals are presented as naturally content and at ease.

questions.question: What does the poem suggest about human society?

options.B: It is full of dissatisfaction, greed and anxiety
options.D: It is exactly like animal society

questions.explanation: The poet contrasts human complications with the calm life he observes in animals.

questions.question: Why does the poet mention “sins” and “deeds”?

options.A: To explain the history of religion
options.C: To show that humans often worry about moral judgment and their actions
options.D: To discuss religious rules in detail

questions.explanation: These references highlight human guilt, anxiety and self-consciousness.

questions.question: What does the poet mean by saying animals do not “lie awake in the dark and weep for their sins”?

options.C: Animals are not burdened by human-style guilt and moral anxiety

questions.explanation: The poet emphasizes that animals do not experience the same self-conscious guilt as humans.

questions.question: What does the poet’s admiration of animals reveal about his attitude toward human life?

options.A: He is frustrated by some complexities and artificial desires of human life
options.C: He wants animals to become human

questions.explanation: The poem expresses dissatisfaction with certain human habits and a longing for simplicity.

questions.question: What is the main contrast in the poem?
questions.explanation: The poem repeatedly contrasts the calm contentment of animals with human dissatisfaction.

questions.question: What does the poet mean when he says animals do not “sweat and whine about their condition”?

options.A: Animals do not complain constantly about their circumstances

questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes the animals’ acceptance of their natural condition.

questions.question: Why does the poet say animals do not “kneel to another” or show reverence to their kind?

options.A: Animals are afraid of one another
options.D: He sees animals as free from the social hierarchies and false displays common among humans

questions.explanation: The poet contrasts animal equality and natural behaviour with human social pretensions.

questions.question: What is suggested by the poet’s statement that animals do not “own things”?

options.D: Animals are free from the human obsession with possession and materialism

questions.explanation: The poet sees freedom from material possession as one reason for their contentment.

questions.question: What does the poet’s longing to live with animals most strongly represent?

options.A: A plan to keep wild animals at home
options.B: A desire to escape human complexity and return to a simpler, more natural way of living
options.D: A wish to become a zoologist

questions.explanation: His wish symbolizes a longing for simplicity, contentment and freedom from artificial human concerns.

questions.question: Which statement best expresses the deeper message of “Animals”?

options.A: Animals are more intelligent than humans in every way
options.B: Humans should literally abandon society and live with wild animals
options.D: The poem questions human greed, dissatisfaction and anxiety by contrasting them with the apparent contentment of animals

questions.explanation: The poem uses animals as a contrast to encourage reflection on human desires, dissatisfaction and unnecessary complications.

questions.question: How does the fog move?

questions.question: What does the fog sit on?

questions.question: What does the phrase “little cat feet” mainly suggest?

questions.question: What atmosphere does the poem create?

questions.question: Why is the poem so short?

questions.question: What does “sits on silent haunches” suggest?

questions.question: What happens after the fog has watched the harbour and city?

questions.question: What is the effect of personifying the fog as a cat?

options.D: It gives the fog a scientific explanation

questions.question: Which contrast is suggested by the poem?

questions.question: Why is the cat image particularly effective in the poem?

questions.question: What does the fog's brief stay suggest about nature?

options.A: Cities are permanently covered by fog
options.C: Cats and fog are scientifically related

poems.title: The Tale of Custard the Dragon

questions.question: Who is the poet of “The Tale of Custard the Dragon”?
questions.explanation: Ogden Nash wrote this humorous narrative poem.

questions.question: Who is Belinda?
questions.explanation: Belinda is the girl who lives in a little white house with her pets.

questions.question: Where does Belinda live?
questions.explanation: The poem introduces Belinda as living in a little white house.

questions.question: Which animal is described as a little black kitten?
questions.explanation: Ink is Belinda's little black kitten.

questions.question: Who is Mustard?
questions.explanation: Mustard is Belinda's yellow dog.

questions.question: Who is Blink?
questions.explanation: Blink is the little grey mouse who lives with Belinda.

questions.question: Who is Custard?
questions.explanation: Custard is Belinda's pet dragon.

questions.question: What did Custard always ask for?
questions.explanation: Custard is portrayed as timid and repeatedly asks for a safe cage.

questions.question: What did Belinda and her other pets claim to be?
questions.explanation: Belinda and the other pets boast about their bravery.

questions.question: Who suddenly enters Belinda's house?
questions.explanation: A pirate enters the house carrying weapons, creating the danger that tests everyone's bravery.

questions.question: Why did Belinda and her pets laugh at Custard?

options.B: He was timid and asked for a safe cage

questions.explanation: Custard was considered cowardly because he repeatedly wanted a safe place.

questions.question: What did Belinda claim about herself?
questions.explanation: Belinda and the other pets proudly claimed that they were brave.

questions.question: What did the pirate carry when he entered the house?
questions.explanation: The pirate is described as carrying weapons, making him a serious threat.

questions.question: How did Belinda react when the pirate appeared?
questions.explanation: Belinda became frightened and called for help.

questions.question: What did Mustard do when he saw the pirate?
questions.explanation: Mustard, who had claimed to be brave, became frightened when faced with real danger.

questions.question: What happened to Ink and Blink when the pirate appeared?
questions.explanation: The supposedly brave pets were frightened by the pirate.

questions.question: What did Custard do when everyone else was afraid?
questions.explanation: Custard unexpectedly showed real courage by confronting the pirate.

questions.question: What happened to the pirate?
questions.explanation: Custard defeated the pirate and swallowed him.

questions.question: What did the other characters do after Custard defeated the pirate?

options.B: They claimed that they could have defeated the pirate themselves

questions.explanation: Even after Custard's brave act, the others continued boasting about their own bravery.

questions.question: What important contrast is central to the poem?
questions.explanation: The characters who appear brave prove cowardly, while timid-looking Custard demonstrates real courage.

questions.question: What does Custard's behaviour during the pirate's attack reveal?

options.A: He was pretending to be weak all the time
options.B: He was stronger because he was a dragon
options.C: Real courage can appear when a person faces actual danger

questions.explanation: Custard had always appeared timid, but when danger actually came, he faced the pirate.
